extraction.name: CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
extraction.description: CADS is an open-source framework and large-scale dataset comprising 22,022 CT volumes with complete annotations for 167 anatomical structures, designed for whole-body CT segmentation.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset aggregates CT scans from 40 diverse sources, including public archives (TCIA, Grand Challenge, MICCAI), research studies, and newly acquired hospital cohorts. Data was collected between 2007 and 2024 from over 100 imaging facilities across 16 countries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 79% of the initial collection lacked any manual annotations. Only 21% of images had partial annotations from public sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources, including public archives (e.g., TCIA, TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K), medical imaging challenges, and newly acquired anonymized head and abdominal CT scans.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data was standardized by aligning images to RAS orientation and resampling to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution. Affine matrices were simplified. Facial features in new head CTs were anonymized using a Gaussian filter. Pseudo-labels were generated and refined through shape-based quality control and ensemble selection.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were reoriented to RAS convention, resampled to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and affine matrices were simplified. For evaluation, model outputs were adapted to match dataset annotation schemes (e.g., merging structures).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were generated using a multi-stage pipeline: 1) Specialized models trained on fully annotated subsets generated pseudo-labels for all 167 structures. 2) Shape-informed quality control using neural implicit functions filtered unreliable pseudo-labels. 3) Multi-strategy label generation via ensemble selection of three model flavors (GT, Pseudo, Shape). 4) Final labels assembled by prioritizing GT annotations and merging pseudo-labels based on reliability. Manual annotations were added for specific OARs on VISCERAL Gold Corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Expert radiation oncologists reviewed segmentations for clinical accuracy. A curated test set was created by excluding structures with unreliable ground truth annotations identified through medical professional review. Disagreements and errors in existing datasets (e.g., TotalSegmentator) were documented and corrected.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: In-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist performed manual annotations. Expert radiation oncologists (5.5 years experience) performed clinical validation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net, PyTorch, Seg-metrics, surface-distance, TPTBox, vesselFM, ANTS
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, models, and code are publicly available on Hugging Face and GitHub. No specific versioning or update schedule is mentioned beyond the initial release.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: CT scans contain anatomical data. Facial features in newly acquired head CTs were anonymized using a Gaussian filter to protect patient identity.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance robust AI solutions in radiology, making comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers. It supports applications in radiation therapy planning, diagnosis, and research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset spans diverse populations and imaging protocols but is limited to data from 16 countries. Exclusion of low-quality pseudo-labels may limit learning of pathological edge cases. Facial anonymization limits detailed facial analysis.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Exclusion of low-quality pseudo-labels may remove pathological cases. Coverage is limited to head-to-knee. Some structures (e.g., trachea wall, heart superior portions) are under-segmented or imprecise. Facial anonymization limits facial analysis applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Use cases include whole-body CT segmentation, radiation therapy planning, organ volume quantification, and medical image analysis research.
